_readme: One reward track per character: the forty-level rail on the reward-track screen, levels 2-40 (RewardTrack.StartingLevel/MaxLevel; level 1 is where a character starts, not somewhere they arrive). EVERY LEVEL IS AUTHORED. A track used to be DESCRIBED -- twelve milestones plus a 'filler' mix of (reward, amount, count) rows the game spread across the levels nobody had named -- and progression v2 phase 4 replaced that with one 'levels' array carrying an explicit entry for every level from 2 to 40, because the table in docs/handoffs/progression_v2/PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md section 4 is nothing but placements and a computed placement cannot express one. A character with no entry in 'tracks' gets RewardTrackDefinition.Default instead -- Bump/Choice alternating, Respec at 8, Second Life at 25, Identity above 30 -- so an undesigned character still shows a plain, honest track rather than a blank or broken one. THE THREE VALIDATION RULES RewardTrackEntryResolver enforces: (1) every level from 2 to RewardTrack.MaxLevel carries exactly one entry and no entry names a level outside that span; (2) a one-shot capability -- Respec, SecondLife, SignatureAbsorbs, UnlockSkill -- appears at most once (UnlockSkill keyed by its own skillId, so two levels naming two different skills both count, but the same skill twice does not), because HasUnlocked only ever asks whether the FIRST level a capability appears at has been reached; (3) a signature reward (SignatureCapacity/GainPerTurn/GainOnDamageTaken/AbsorbPerPoint) is refused on a character with no signatureId, because BuildSignatureResource would have nothing to pay it into. ON TOP OF THOSE, RewardTrackNodeValidation checks the SHAPE of the combat stretch: no two neighbouring nodes between 2 and 30 share a kind, an Ability at 3/10/20 is followed by a Choice, everything above 30 is Identity, a Choice is worth exactly 4, and the five authored Bump floors hold (MaxHealth 30, MaxMana 6, elemental/spell damage 5, a Fury gain step 5, signature gain per turn 1). MILESTONE LEVELS -- 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 38, 40 -- are shared by every track and are a SCREEN fact, not a content one: the screen bakes milestone-ness (disc size, ring sprite, caption font) into the built scene, so only the CONTENT at each level is per-character. reward is a TrackReward enum member name, matched case-insensitively; against is a DamageType name (Ice, not the skill-JSON-only alias Frost), read only by ElementalDamagePercent; skillId is read by UnlockSkill and by the three Skill*Delta kinds and must name a real skill id -- the track's skill branch carries no ownership test, so a track may grant a skill authored to a different character (docs/PLAN_REWARD_TRACKS.md sections 3f/3h), which is what lets Odette's track hand her the book spells all authored characterId 'sheep'. resource is a TrackResourceTarget (Mana or Signature) and is read only by SkillCostDelta; identityKind and value are read only by Identity. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md. The design these three tracks implement, level by level: docs/handoffs/progression_v2/PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md sections 4 and 5.

tracks._comment: SHAWN, THE WOOL ECONOMY -- PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md section 4's first column, with section 5's own explanation of what each bump changes at the level it lands: Wool per turn 1 to 2 at 5 (Shear, 3 Wool, every other turn instead of every third); Shear 3 to 2 at 12 (with 2 a turn, Shear every turn); +2 Wool when hurt at 19 (two hits taken fund a Shear); Battering Ram 6 to 4 at 24 (affordable after two turns instead of three). Level 15 is TUCK IN, an Ability node rather than a Capability: phase 1 measured the automatic Wool absorb this slot originally held and rejected it (Shear starvation 41% at baseline to 55% with it, PHASE1_BOT_REPORT.md section b), so the node became a skill the player presses. The ability-then-choice rule still holds, because 16 is a Choice. Level 26 raises Tuck In's ward from 2 per Wool to 3 through SkillPowerDelta -- `power`, the per-point lever, not `flatAmount`. Level 30 is the owner-designed fourth ability and is a PLACEHOLDER (placeholder_shawn_capstone in skills.json carries the note): the node exists on the rail so the shape of the track is real, and what it grants is not designed yet.

BJORN, THE FURY CURVE -- PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md section 4's second column. The four Fury nodes are the whole of his progression's shape and section 5 states what each one changes: 20 per attack at 5 reaches the x2 tier in 3 attacks instead of 4; opening at 25 at 15 makes it 2; 25 per attack at 19 makes it 1; opening at 50 at 26 makes the x2 Slam the opening move of every fight. FuryGainOnAttack and FuryStartOfFight are SET, not summed -- the table says '15 to 20' then '20 to 25', which are two totals -- so the higher collected value wins rather than the two adding. NO SIGNATURE REWARD ANYWHERE: he has no signatureId, and rule 3 refuses one. No MaxMana or ManaRegen either -- fury's capacityRule is Fixed and it is not restoredByManaEffects, so both would resolve clean and pay nothing (AUDIT #145). Slam's two +5 flat nodes at 12 and 24 replace revision 1's third gain bump, which phase 1 found dead at the breakpoints: base 27 to 32 to 37, felt on every slam and multiplied by whichever tier fired.

ODETTE, THE ELEMENTALIST -- PLAN_PROGRESSION_V2.md section 4's third column. Her mana economy is the spine: the orb costs 8, 36 mana at 5 is 4 casts instead of 3, cost 7 at 15 is 5, 42 mana at 17 is 6, cost 6 at 26 is 7. SpellCostDelta is SET rather than summed for the same reason the Fury nodes are -- '1 less' then '2 less' are two totals. THE THREE DAMAGE NODES ARE SpellDamagePercent, not per-element: revision 2 replaced her per-element bumps because +5% to everything she casts is build-agnostic, and because the format carries one entry per level and 'every element' cannot be authored as ten rows at one level. Her three UnlockSkill nodes name book spells -- frost_flare, lightning_bolt -- authored characterId 'sheep' because that is who they were drafted for; the track has no ownership test, which is the point (sections 3f/3h). A book the track has handed over stops being offered in the shop (RunOrchestrator.AvailableBookOptions).
